Proposed Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendments for Quayside Master Plan Blocks 3b, 4 and 5. The proposal for Blocks 3b, 4 and 5 includes two residential towers and one mid-rise building, collectively accommodating 8,988 square metres of non-residential Gross Floor Area (GFA) and 119,581 square metres of residential GFA. The residential component includes 1,475 condo units and 407 affordable units. The buildings will flank a portion of a 14,350 square metre east-west "Community Forest" which is continuous through the centre of the broader development. The mid-rise building on Block 3B will also support portion of a rooftop urban farm, which extends the length of the mid-rise buildings on Blocks 1, 2 and 3b connected by a suspended pedestrian bridge across Small Street.  An application is required to amend the City of Toronto Official Plan to permit additional height and density and an application to amend the former City of Toronto Zoning By-law 438-86, as amended by OMB-approved By-law 1174-2010, is required to permit additional height and density, amend the permitted uses, update zoning maps and revise certain zoning standards to permit the proposed development. This application forms part of the broader Quayside Master Plan, which is comprised of seven mixed use buildings on four development blocks and public realm improvements on the interior and perimiter of the site. The development includes 321,760 square metres of GFA allotted as 22,562 square metres of commercial, retail, institutional and other non-residential uses and 299,209 square metres of residential uses supporting 4,634 condo units and 869 affordable housing units. Public realm and infrastructure works to be delivered by Waterfront Toronto include the Queens Quay East extension, plazas at Parliament Street and Queens Quay East, an extended Water's Edge Promenade and a 0.4 hectare park.

The East Harbour Transit Oriented Community (TOC) proposal was approved in 2022 through a Minister's Zoning Order (MZO-O.Reg. 329/22) as part of the Provincial Transit Oriented Communities Program. The MZO introduced 302,000 sqm of residential permissions to the existing 926,000 sqm of non-residential, for a total of 1,228,000 sqm of development permissions. The addition of residential permissions is a change from the approved planning framework completed in 2018 which envisions an office employment hub. The proposal comprises 9 office towers ranging from 31-48 storeys in height, and 9 residential towers ranging from 23-65 storeys in height, adjacent to the future East Harbour transit hub. Public consultation for the East Harbour TOC proposal was proponent-led. It included 3 Local Advisory Committee (LAC) meetings, 4 virtual Open House and 14,000 information mailer-sheets to residents in adjacent communities, directing them to the consultation website, called 'Engage East Harbour'. City staff and the local Councillor participated in all public consultation sessions hosted by the developer, Cadillac Fairview.This application is related to the subdivision application 16 270078 STE 30 SB which was approved in 2024.

The development includes 321,760 square metres of GFA allotted as 22,562 square metres of commercial, retail, institutional and other non-residential uses and 299,209 square metres of residential uses supporting 4,634 condo units and 869 affordable housing units. Public realm and infrastructure works to be delivered by Waterfront Toronto include the Queens Quay East extension, plazas at Parliament Street and Queens Quay East, an extended Water's Edge Promenade and a 0.4 hectare park.

The East Harbour Transit Oriented Community (TOC) proposal was approved in 2022 through a Minister's Zoning Order (MZO-O.Reg. 329/22) as part of the Provincial Transit Oriented Communities Program. The MZO introduced 302,000 sqm of residential permissions to the existing 926,000 sqm of non-residential, for a total of 1,228,000 sqm of development permissions. The addition of residential permissions is a change from the approved planning framework completed in 2018 which envisions an office employment hub. The proposal comprises 9 office towers ranging from 31-48 storeys in height, and 9 residential towers ranging from 23-65 storeys in height, adjacent to the future East Harbour transit hub. Public consultation for the East Harbour TOC proposal was proponent-led. It included 3 Local Advisory Committee (LAC) meetings, 4 virtual Open House and 14,000 information mailer-sheets to residents in adjacent communities, directing them to the consultation website, called 'Engage East Harbour'. City staff and the local Councillor participated in all public consultation sessions hosted by the developer, Cadillac Fairview.This application is related to the subdivision application 16 270078 STE 30 SB which was approved in 2024.

The proposed development includes a number of mid-rise and tall buildings, ranging in height from 28-storeys on Bathurst Street, and stepping down toward the south and west. A total of 23 of the 27 listed heritage buildings on the site are being retained and incorporated into the development. The revised proposal comprises a total of 804 residential units in 59,883 square metres of residential floor area, and 15,253 square metres of new non-residential uses. The overall density of the proposal is FSI of 5.69 times the site, inclusive of retained heritage buildings, and 5.29 times the area of the site, exclusive of retained heritage buildings. The City received an application to amend the Zoning By-law to permit a new high-rise residential building in the northwest corner of a 1.26 hectare site with two existing high-rise rental apartment buildings. The application was approved in principle by the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal (LPAT) following a settlement hearing and pursuant to an Order/Decision dated September 12, 2019. The LPAT-approved building is proposed to be 31-storeys (99 metres including mechanical penthouse) in height. The new building would include 263 dwelling units, 659 square metres of indoor amenity space and 278 square metres of outdoor amenity space. The application also includes new parkland in the south portion of the site on the north side Jackes Avenue and in close proximity to David A. Balfour Park, a new 581 square metre amenity pavilion along the eastern lot line which would be accessible to tenants of both the existing and proposed building, renovations to the amenity areas within each of the existing buildings, and overall site improvements.

ZBA application 21 169458 NNY 15 OZ (for 124 Broadway Ave) and ZBA application 21 234009 NNY 15 OZ (for 136 Broadway Ave) have been submitted to permit a development containing two towers atop a shared podium. Each property will contain one tower and the shared podium will span across the two sites. Shared vehicular access will be provided on the east side of 136 Broadway Avenue. The tower at 124 Broadway Ave is proposed to be 36 storeys tall (114.45m + 6m MPH). The tower at 136 Broadway Ave is proposed to be 30 storeys (96.6m + 6m MPH). The existing 86 rental units on 124 Broadway and 39 rental units on 136 Broadway will be replaced within the tower at 136 Broadway Avenue. In addition, the applicant agreed to provide 50 net new affordable rental units in the building at 136 Broadway Avenue.

This application proposes to amend the Official Plan and Zoning By-laws to permit a phased multi-block mixed use development consisting of five residential apartment buildings having a total of 123,653 m2 of gross floor area, of which 952 m2 would be for non-residential uses.  The proposed buildings would range in height from 6 to 8-storeys along Portland Street; 12-storeys located internal to the subject site, along Audley Street and along the southern property line; and have tall buildings with heights of 16, 23, 25 and 32-storeys oriented towards the southern portion of the lands.  The development would contain approximately 1,824 residential units and a total of 1,049 vehicular parking spaces and 1,278 bicycle parking spaces. This application is for site plan control to permit two residential apartment buildings of 28 and 30 storeys for a total of 612 dwelling units.  Also proposed are an additional 26 three-storey townhouse units.  There are a total of 632 parking spaces proposed with 537 for residents and 95 for visitors.  Parking for the towers is proposed within a 4-level below grade parking garage.  The development will be constructed in 3 phases with phase I consisting of the 28-storey tower (329 units) plus 13 townhouses.  Phase II will include the 30-storey building (283 units) and phase III will include 13 townhouse units.  An east-west 18.5 metre public road is also proposed.

Resubmission received on September 21, 2016: The Applicant has submitted a revised OPA/Rezoning Application # 15 256717 STE 30 OZ and Site Plan Application # 15 256718 STE 30 SA for the lands at 1117 and 1119 Gerrard Street East. The site is currently developed with a Place of Worship (the former Riverdale United Church) at 1117 Gerrard Street East and an existing five-storey apartment building containing 29 alternative housing rental units. The development applications submitted to the City contemplate the demolition of the existing Place of Worship, and to redevelop the lands for a five-storey building, containing 35 new alternative housing units, generally intended for low-income seniors, and approximately 235 square metres of community centre space (Parent Resource Centre) at-grade. The owner is also intending to add a new rental unit to the existing 29 unit, five-storey building at 1119 Gerrard Street East, thus bringing the total new rental units through this development application to 36 (1 new unit at 1119 Gerrard Street East and 35 new units at 1117 Gerrard Street East). The 36 new rental units will replace 36 rent-geared-to-income units at 835-841 Queen Street East, which is currently subject to a rental housing demolition application (File # 14 153558 STE 30 RH) through Section 111 of the City of Toronto Act, 2006.

Enbridge Gas Distribution Inc. ("EGO") leases a 40.94m2 portion of land from the City of Toronto, which is located within Woodbine Park in the City of Toronto. EGO has been leasing the lands for over 20 years. The lands are designated in the Official Plan as Park, and the City of Toronto - Real Estate Services division has indicated that a lease renewal on the subject lands would be considered a disposal of Parks and Open Space lands as per Section 4.3.8 of the Official Plan. In order to rectify this matter, the City of Toronto Real Estate Services division has requested that EGO apply for a Site Specific Official Plan Amendment. An exemption of the leased lands from Section 4.3.8 of the Official Plan would allow the City of Toronto to renew EGO's lease of the subject lands.

Revised Application Submitted on December 15, 2017: The Applicant, Belleterre Real Estate Partners Limited, has submitted a revised application for Site Plan Control, which proposes the development of a 5-storey, 13,447 m2, self-storage warehouse (Storage Warehouse, Class A) over two phases of construction. Loading docks for the proposed storage use will be provided and will be located internal to the proposed building. A 371 m2 Designer's Studio is proposed to be located on the ground floor of the 5-storey building. A total of 40 parking spaces, 6 bicycle parking spaces, and 4 loading spaces are proposed to serve the development. The site has a total area of 18,245 m2; however, the development will be located only on the northern portion of the site, which maintains an area of 6,638 m2. Please note that the site is subject to the Lower Don Special Policy Area. Also note that the approval for this site plan now rests with the Ontario Municipal Board (OMB). The OMB issued a decision on July 4, 2016 (Case # MM150067) allowing the development to proceed in its proposed location, and issued a subsequent oral decision on July 27, 2017, requesting to resolve this matter within 20 business days of final site plan submission to City staff. As Planning and Legal staff have been directed to respond to the OMB with a full and final NOAC, please ensure your comments include final pre- and post-approval conditions.

Resubmission received on September 21, 2016: The Applicant has submitted a revised OPA/Rezoning Application # 15 256717 STE 30 OZ and Site Plan Application # 15 256718 STE 30 SA for the lands at 1117 and 1119 Gerrard Street East. The site is currently developed with a Place of Worship (the former Riverdale United Church) at 1117 Gerrard Street East and an existing five-storey apartment building containing 29 alternative housing rental units. The development applications submitted to the City contemplate the demolition of the existing Place of Worship, and to redevelop the lands for a five-storey building, containing 35 new alternative housing units, generally intended for low-income seniors, and approximately 235 square metres of community centre space (Parent Resource Centre) at-grade. The owner is also intending to add a new rental unit to the existing 29 unit, five-storey building at 1119 Gerrard Street East, thus bringing the total new rental units through this development application to 36 (1 new unit at 1119 Gerrard Street East and 35 new units at 1117 Gerrard Street East). The 36 new rental units will replace 36 rent-geared-to-income units at 835-841 Queen Street East, which is currently subject to a rental housing demolition application (File # 14 153558 STE 30 RH) through Section 111 of the City of Toronto Act, 2006.

This Official Plan Amendment application proposes that the City grant a permanent easement to Toronto Hydro Electric System Limited (Toronto Hydro) in order to permit Toronto Hydro to continue to use a portion of City owned parklands at 300 MacPherson Avenue and 235 Cottingham Street for below grade electrical services that were installed in 2014. A temporary short term easement  was previously granted for a two year period pending determinations as to final approval. An Official Plan Amendment is required to proceed because the property is designated as Parks and Open Space Areas under the Toronto Official Plan. The sale or disposal of City owned Parks and Open Space Areas is prohibited by Official Plan policies and the granting of an easement exceeding a period of 21 years is a form of disposal that is not permitted.

The original application included three conceptual block master plan options that comprised of a range of retail, office, hotel and residential uses with a maximum proposed total future gross floor area of 682,670 square metres and 2.29 Floor Space Index and an internal private above and below grade street network. The application has been revised into a single concept with expanded parkland and the inclusion of a public road. The proposal continues to propose a range of uses, including affordable housing which is intended to occur in a phased manner over the next 20+ years

Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment applications to permit three new buildings on the lands, comprising a 58-storey mixed-use condominium building with 4,060 square metres of non-residential uses in the lower floors and 741 dwelling units, a 21-storey purpose built rental building with 287 dwelling units with 310 square metres of community space, and a 9-storey purpose built rental building with 81 dwelling units. The proposal also includes 18 replacement rental units, of which the exact location remains to be determined. A 3,135 square metre parkland conveyance plus a 772 square metre Stratified Public Park Area and enhanced open spaces with a range of programming across the site are proposed. A new public street, which would extend Rose Avenue through to the northern boundary of the site and a series of private streets across the site are proposed. The proposal includes modifications to the layout and uses within the existing buildings to create new amenity and non-residential spaces, which would result in the loss of 18 existing rental dwelling units that would be replaced elsewhere within the site as determined though the development review. The remaining 2,251 rental dwelling units are proposed to be retained, along with 1,828 square metres of existing non-residential space. The existing and proposed buildings would result in 3,360 dwelling units with a gross floor area of 231,028 square metres, and 6,198 square metres of non-residential gross floor area, for a total gross floor area of 237,226 square metres across the site.

To permit the redevelopment of the 60 acre subject site into a new community  consisting of: office buildings (including the retention of the Celestica headquarters); commercial and retail space; 4,921 residential units within a range of building types including tall buildings, mid-rise buildings and low-rise town houses; land for a community centre, new public roads, open spaces and parks.The proposal will be developed in phases, in conjunction with the Don Mills Crossing Study. The Study is a comprehensive review of the anticipated growth around the intersection of Don Mills Road and Eglinton Avenue East and builds on the work of Eglinton Connects. The Study  will result in a new planning framework which will include implementation measures to support co-ordinated development of employment, residential and community uses. The current application is a revision to the May 2014 Official Plan Amendment application (14 153614 NNY 26 OZ) and submission of new Zoning By-law Amendment and Draft Plan of Subdivision applications.

A draft plan of subdivision application will follow in the near future to create the proposed development blocks, the roads and the public park.

Phase 2B: Castlepoint Numa has filed an application for Site Plan Control. The application seeks site plan approval for a one-storey building used for communication and broadcasting in the Pinewood Toronto Studios campus within the Port Lands. The building is currently built, having benefited from a temporary building permit issued by Toronto Buildings. The site plan process will secure the building for a longer time period than what a temporary building permit can provide, which is typically between 6 months to a year. The proposed building is situated on lands that will be part of the future Broadview Extension, and as such will need to be demolished at a certain point in the future to accommodate the Broadview Extension. The applicant acknowledges this requirement and it will be reflected in the Notice of Approval Conditions.

INACTIVE Site Plan Control application to permit the proposed Humber Cultural Hub which is a phased institutional development as part of the Humber College Lakeshore Campus. The proposal includes the partial redevelopment of the existing building with the construction of multiple building additions that would be developed in two phases. The first phase would include the construction of an 8 student residence building that would be connected by 1 to 4-storey academic podiums. The second phase would include a new 3-storey academic podium, with a music and performing arts hall, which would connect to the first phase. The existing 6-storey student residence fronting Lake Shore Boulevard West would remain, as well as the existing 2 and 3-storey library building which would connect to the proposed development. The existing 2-storey academic building component located in the center of the site would be demolished and a portion of the existing surface parking lot would be removed to facilitate the proposal.The total gross floor area of the institutional development would be 49,611 m², of which 30,380 m² would be attributed to the proposed development and 19,231 m² would be attributed to the existing buildings that would be retained on the site.

The original application proposed a zoning by-law amendment and sought rental housing demolition and replacement approval to permit the redevelopment of the site with a total of 886 residential units ranging in buildings from 10 to 32 storeys in height, ground floor retail and a public parkette.  The second submission proposed the demolition of the two existing apartment buildings and the redevelopment of the site with a total of 842 residential units.  This included 33 stacked townhouses on the east side of the site, plus three buildings, one of which would contain ground floor retail, would range in height from 12 to 28 storeys and would contain 663 condominium units.  A public park fronting Brimorton Drive is also proposed.  The 141 rental units would be replaced with 146 rental units in a new 16 storey building.  This revised submission reduces the building heights of the two buildings fronting Markham Road from 28 storeys to 24 storeys, which reduces the number of units in these two buildings from 553 to 473.  The revised rental replacement building will provide 29 three bedroom units and will also provide five, family oriented, grade accessible units located on the ground floor.  As a result of the changes, the overall unit count has been reduced to 762 dwelling units.

Zoning By Law Amendment and concurrent Draft Plan of Subdvision applications to create 13 blocks within the William Baker Neighbourhood. Planned as new inclusive, compact and complete community that is walkable and well served by transit and active transportation. The Neighbourhood is intended to be developed over phases with a broad range and mix of uses, built forms, densities, housing and unit types and tenures (including affordable and seniors options), all supported by an existing higher order transit and existing and planned community services and facilities. The District Plan for the William Baker Neighbourhood includes development blocks at the south end proposed for a mix of high/mid and low-rise residential as well as mixed use blocks at the intersection of Keele Street and Sheppard Avenue, to create a Neighbourhood Focus at that gateway to the community featuring commercial uses and parks, in a location well served by transit. Building heights in this area are proposed to range from 4 to 20 storeys. Residential blocks proposed in the north portion, which will be developed through subsequent phases, provide for similar heights in the range of 4 to 20 storeys, with potential for some taller elements near the Downsview Park subway/GO station hub. Of great importance to the future of the Neighbourhood is preservation and enhancement of the woodlot. It will be a central feature of the new community and further enhanced with additional parkland being added around its edges as contemplated by the Secondary Plan. Additionally, a park at the southern end of the Neighbourhood is proposed to feature a new pedestrian/cycling bridge that will provide a convenient link to Downsview Park to the south.

Zoning By Law Amendment and concurrent Draft Plan of Subdvision applications to create 13 blocks within the William Baker Neighbourhood. Planned as new inclusive, compact and complete community that is walkable and well served by transit and active transportation. The Neighbourhood is intended to be developed over phases with a broad range and mix of uses, built forms, densities, housing and unit types and tenures (including affordable and seniors options), all supported by an existing higher order transit and existing and planned community services and facilities. The District Plan for the William Baker Neighbourhood includes development blocks at the south end proposed for a mix of high/mid and low-rise residential as well as mixed use blocks at the intersection of Keele Street and Sheppard Avenue, to create a Neighbourhood Focus at that gateway to the community featuring commercial uses and parks, in a location well served by transit. Building heights in this area are proposed to range from 4 to 20 storeys. Residential blocks proposed in the north portion, which will be developed through subsequent phases, provide for similar heights in the range of 4 to 20 storeys, with potential for some taller elements near the Downsview Park subway/GO station hub. Of great importance to the future of the Neighbourhood is preservation and enhancement of the woodlot. It will be a central feature of the new community and further enhanced with additional parkland being added around its edges as contemplated by the Secondary Plan. Additionally, a park at the southern end of the Neighbourhood is proposed to feature a new pedestrian/cycling bridge that will provide a convenient link to Downsview Park to the south.

The East Harbour Transit Oriented Community (TOC) proposal was approved in 2022 through a Minister's Zoning Order (MZO-O.Reg. 329/22) as part of the Provincial Transit Oriented Communities Program. The MZO introduced 302,000 sqm of residential permissions to the existing 926,000 sqm of non-residential, for a total of 1,228,000 sqm of development permissions. The addition of residential permissions is a change from the approved planning framework completed in 2018 which envisions an office employment hub. The proposal comprises 9 office towers ranging from 31-48 storeys in height, and 9 residential towers ranging from 23-65 storeys in height, adjacent to the future East Harbour transit hub. Public consultation for the East Harbour TOC proposal was proponent-led. It included 3 Local Advisory Committee (LAC) meetings, 4 virtual Open House and 14,000 information mailer-sheets to residents in adjacent communities, directing them to the consultation website, called 'Engage East Harbour'. City staff and the local Councillor participated in all public consultation sessions hosted by the developer, Cadillac Fairview.This application is related to the subdivision application 16 270078 STE 30 SB which was approved in 2024.

Zoning By Law Amendment and concurrent Draft Plan of Subdvision applications to create 13 blocks within the William Baker Neighbourhood. Planned as new inclusive, compact and complete community that is walkable and well served by transit and active transportation. The Neighbourhood is intended to be developed over phases with a broad range and mix of uses, built forms, densities, housing and unit types and tenures (including affordable and seniors options), all supported by an existing higher order transit and existing and planned community services and facilities. The District Plan for the William Baker Neighbourhood includes development blocks at the south end proposed for a mix of high/mid and low-rise residential as well as mixed use blocks at the intersection of Keele Street and Sheppard Avenue, to create a Neighbourhood Focus at that gateway to the community featuring commercial uses and parks, in a location well served by transit. Building heights in this area are proposed to range from 4 to 20 storeys. Residential blocks proposed in the north portion, which will be developed through subsequent phases, provide for similar heights in the range of 4 to 20 storeys, with potential for some taller elements near the Downsview Park subway/GO station hub. Of great importance to the future of the Neighbourhood is preservation and enhancement of the woodlot. It will be a central feature of the new community and further enhanced with additional parkland being added around its edges as contemplated by the Secondary Plan. Additionally, a park at the southern end of the Neighbourhood is proposed to feature a new pedestrian/cycling bridge that will provide a convenient link to Downsview Park to the south.

The proposed development will maintain a predominantly mid-scale built form character with an option for two tall buildings of 19 and 23 storeys. Adaptive reuse of buildings from the previous aerospace manufacturing operations will accommodate a range of new institutional, retail, entertainment, and community uses. A range of housing options are proposed including affordable housing. 930 square metres of GFA are proposed for community uses along with a 1,547 square metre child care facility (1,001m indoor; 546 outdoor). The district plan proposes 14,295 square metres of public parkland across 3 parks, 13,844 square metres of privately-owned publicly accessible spaces, and 9,103 square metres of greenways.

The applicant's concept plan proposes two condominium apartment buildings of 13 and 12 storeys having a total of 276 dwelling units and a maximum height of approximately 44 metres (144 feet) located on the western portion of the site.  These buildings would be connected by a 2-storey lobby and common amenity building and include 1,065 m2 of commercial space on the ground floors of the two towers.  Proposed on the eastern portion of the site are 30 three storey townhouse units in 6 blocks.  A total of 314 residential parking spaces are proposed of which 35 would be dedicated for visitors.  Parking for the towers would be provided in a multi-level below grade parking garage having 284 spaces and 30 parking spaces would be provided within at-grade garages for the townhouses.  The development is proposed to be served by private streets with access provided from a driveway off Tippett Road.

Bousfields Inc. has submitted an application for Zoning By-law Amendment.  The application proposes three mixed-use buildings with heights of 25, 30 and 37 storeys. The proposed development would be deployed in 2 phases with phase 1 consisting of the 37-storey building and phase 2 consisting of the 25 and 30 storeys buildings. The application proposes 935 residential units with a mix of unit types resulting in a residential gross floor area of 67,992 square metres. The application also proposes 522 square metres of retail/commercial uses and an overall floor space index of 7.36 times. A total of 742 vehicular and 714 bicycle parking spaces and 3 type G and 6 type C loading spaces would be provided. The proposal would provide a new 930 square-metre public park at the western portion of the site, pedestrian connections and privately-owned publicly accessible open spaces. A related Subdivision Application No. 21 201457 ESC 21 SB to create 4 new blocks has also been submitted by the applicant.

Proposal for three buildings based on an approved Municipal Zoning Order. A total of 997 dwelling units, including 282 affordable rental dwelling units (approximately 28% of the total), a 955 square metre community space and 505 square metres of retail space are proposed. Building A (at the central northern part of the site) is a 34-storey tower with retail space on the ground floor and 314 dwelling units above. Building B (at the central southern part of the site) is a 31-storey tower with the existing machine shop building conserved and integrated into the base of the tower. Building B includes retail space and a community space on the ground floor and 282 affordable rental dwelling units above. Building C (at the northeastern corner of the site) is a 43-storey residential tower that includes 401 dwelling units. The existing cleaning room building at the northwestern corner of the site is proposed to be conserved, with the potential to include non-residential uses, but is not currently identified as part of the proposed development. The MZO is available at https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/200595

The proposal contemplates a new community consisting of nine (9) new mixed-use buildings ranging in height from 30 to 45 storeys. The proposal includes a new 3,267 square metre public park located on the northeast portion of the site, with frontage onto the new public street and the natural feature/natural hazard lands associated with Emery Creek.
